# The reveal's UA-default cancellation lives in consumer stylesheets, not the engine

## Context

Found by shipping the second consumer of the engine reveal and getting a black screen. `#18136` / PR #18137 repairs `apps/workstation`; this is the reason it was breakable at all.

**Live latest-open sweep:** checked the latest 12 open issues at 2026-09-02T18:40Z; no equivalent. `#17739` (closed) covered the reveal's *geometry*, never its layer compositing.

## The Problem

The reveal's contract is split across two realms and only one half is in the engine:

- **The engine owns the animation.** `Neo.main.DomAccess#startViewTransition()` runs `document.startViewTransition()` and animates `::view-transition-new(root)` with a growing `clip-path` circle from `DomUtils.createRevealAnimation()`.
- **A consumer stylesheet owns the cancellation that makes it visible.** The browser cross-fades both snapshots by default; the old layer fades out over ~250ms while the reveal grows for 500ms. Unless the consumer declares `animation: none` (and `mix-blend-mode: normal`, against the UA's `plus-lighter`) on both pseudo-elements, the back half of every reveal paints bare backdrop.

Nothing on the call path says so. The census when the second consumer landed:

| app | calls `startViewTransition` | ships the rule |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/portal` | 1 | 1 |
| `apps/workstation` | 1 | **0** |

I matched the Portal's call byte-for-byte, verified the payload and the produced keyframes at the runtime boundary, and still shipped black — because the missing half is not a call-site property. Consumer #3 will hit it the same way.

## The Architectural Reality

An engine capability that requires an undocumented CSS declaration from each consumer is a half-primitive. The visible behaviour is not a consumer style choice: nothing wants the UA cross-fade **and** the circular reveal at the same moment — they are two designs for one transition — so there is no configuration a consumer would reasonably vary.

The cancellation cannot simply be declared globally by the engine, because a caller with **no** `reveal` gets `createRevealAnimation() === null` and legitimately keeps the UA cross-fade. Whatever ships must apply *only when a reveal is actually running*.

## The Fix — browser-verified JS direction

**Preferred: keep it in JS, where the reveal already lives.** Have `createRevealAnimation()` also return keyframes for the old layer, and have `startViewTransition()` register both — holding `::view-transition-old(root)` at `opacity: 1` for the reveal's duration and setting `mix-blend-mode: normal` on both. No global CSS, no new class, self-contained, and the reveal stops depending on anything the consumer must remember.

**Measured premise (2026-09-04, Chrome 152, visible document):** without consumer transition CSS, the old snapshot opacity decayed to `0.787618` and `0.141623` during a plain transition; a WAAPI old-layer opacity hold kept both samples at `1`. This clears the precedence gate for the JS direction. The implementation must also prove normal compositing, zero-duration reveals and cleanup before a subsequent plain transition.

**Fallback if further browser evidence invalidates it:** the engine stamps a class on `documentElement` for the duration of a reveal transition and ships CSS scoped to it — more moving parts, same effect.

Either way, the consumer rules in `apps/portal` and `apps/workstation` become redundant and should be retired **in the same change**, so the duplication does not simply gain a third copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a consumer that calls `startViewTransition()` with a `reveal` and ships **no** view-transition CSS shows the previous state outside the growing circle, with no black frame.
- [ ] **AC-2** — a caller with **no** `reveal` still gets the UA cross-fade; the cancellation must not leak to plain transitions.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the WAAPI-over-UA precedence premise is measured in a real browser and the result recorded, whichever way it falls; if it fails, the class-scoped alternative ships instead.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the now-redundant rules in `apps/portal/Viewport.scss` and `apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` are removed in the same change, and both apps still read correctly.
- [ ] **AC-5 (real browser)** — read by eye in both apps. Use a visible real-browser transition as the compositing witness; previous harness attempts (`pr-13430` and the comments below) could not run a transition. A stylesheet enumeration alone does not prove the pixels.

## Out of Scope

- The reveal's geometry, duration and easing — correct and unchanged.
- Any change to what `startViewTransition()` returns or when it resolves; `#17739` settled that and awaiting completion would break the capture window.

## Avoided Traps

- **Declaring the cancellation globally in an engine stylesheet.** It would silently kill the UA cross-fade for callers who never asked for a reveal — the same class of defect as this ticket, pointed the other way.
- **Leaving the consumer rules in place "just in case" after the engine fix.** Three copies of a workaround for a fixed bug is how the next reader concludes it is still required.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T13:03:28Z

## Released, not abandoned — AC-3 is unmeasurable from my harness, and I checked rather than assumed

I claimed this and am handing it back **unstarted in the tree**, because the ticket's own gate cannot be satisfied here. Recording what I established so the next agent does not repeat it.

### What I could measure (Chrome 148.0.7778.280, real browser, not headless)

```
document.startViewTransition        : present
element.animate(…, {pseudoElement}) : supported
animate on '::view-transition-old(root)' : accepted, no throw
```

**So the mechanism the preferred fix depends on exists.** `createRevealAnimation()` returning keyframes for the old layer and `startViewTransition()` registering them on the pseudo-element is a shape this engine's target browser can express. That was not certain before — it is one of the two things AC-3 asks about.

### What I could not measure, and why

The remaining half — *does a WAAPI animation registered on the pseudo-element outrank the UA's CSS animation on the same property* — needs a transition to actually run. It cannot:

```
document.visibilityState : "hidden"
document.hidden          : true
startViewTransition()    : InvalidStateError: Transition was aborted because of invalid state
```

Confirmed three times, including after forcing a paint, and the harness reports **"The Browser pane is currently hidden"** independently. `startViewTransition` aborts on a hidden document by spec, so **no sampling of `::view-transition-old(root)`'s computed opacity is possible from here at all** — I never got a single sample, which is different from getting zeros.

This is the same wall AC-5 already names for headless (`pr-13430`), one surface over: my browser is real but never visible.

### Why that blocks the ticket rather than just slowing it

AC-3 is not decoration — it **chooses the shape**. *"if it fails, the class-scoped alternative ships instead."* Implementing the preferred JS fix without it would be shipping the unverified premise the ticket explicitly declines to assume, and implementing the fallback without it would be discarding the simpler design on no evidence. Either way the decision would rest on my reasoning about cascade origins rather than on a browser, which is what the ticket forbids.

### For whoever takes it

The measurement is one page and one script — a visible browser, then sample `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement, '::view-transition-old(root)').opacity` across a running transition, with and without the WAAPI hold. If the samples stay `1` with the hold and decay without it, the preferred fix is sound and the rest is mechanical.

**AC-4 is ready regardless of the outcome:** the redundant consumer rules live in exactly two files — `resources/scss/src/apps/portal/Viewport.scss` and `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` — and both must be retired in the same change so the duplication does not gain a third copy.

🖖 Grace


### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-04T03:26:20Z

Not taking this lane, and the reason is a measurement rather than a preference — recording it so the next seat does not spend the turn I just spent.

**AC-3 is unreachable from an agent browser pane.** I tested rather than assumed. With the dev server up and the tab fronted:

```
{"visibilityState": "hidden", "hidden": true,
 "error": "InvalidStateError: Transition was aborted because of invalid state"}
```

The View Transition API refuses to start in a hidden document by spec, so `document.startViewTransition()` aborts before `.ready` ever resolves. Fronting the tab does not help — the *pane* is hidden, not the tab within it. That means no `getAnimations({subtree: true})` sample is possible, so the WAAPI-over-UA precedence premise cannot be measured here in either direction.

This matters for the ticket's shape rather than just for me: **AC-3 chooses between your two candidate fixes**, so the implementer must be able to run it before writing either. A seat that cannot front a browser will reach the same abort, and the only paths that discharge it are a visible browser session or the operator.

AC-5 ("read by eye in both apps") has the same owner by construction.

Everything else in the ticket is sound and I would have enjoyed it — the census table is the epic's thesis in its clearest form, and the "avoided trap" about leaving the consumer rules in place is the right call. Unassigned and untouched; I have added nothing to it.

— Grace 🖖
